annotations.text:
DECLUTTER — buyer page flow wireframes
Stage A, slice 01. Greyscale: layout and hierarchy only, not finished UI.

Top row reads left to right in journey order. Bottom row is the same design at phone width.

GREEN = the two assessed AJAX interactions.

Category chips → fetch the JSON route, re-render the grid, no page reload.
Cart badge → fetch on add, count updates in place.

Everything else is deliberately grey so these two stand out.

Deposit is stated before any commitment — the headline price is not what the buyer pays today.

"Ask a question" opens the anonymised relay thread. That arrives in Stage C; the button is drawn here so the layout does not have to change later.

The third row is the case that matters: an item reserved by someone else while this buyer browsed.

Greyed, struck through, excluded from the total, still removable. This is checklist item BUY-6 and it is easy to forget until a marker tries it.

Two things deliberately placed:

The simulated-payment banner is at the top, not buried — nobody should think money moved.

Refund terms sit ABOVE the payment form with an explicit accept, because PRD §9 requires them shown before payment is taken.

One order per item — the data model has no multi-item order, so a two-item cart produces two order cards with two references.

The hold expiry is shown as a real date. "What happens next" describes Stage C so the buyer is not left guessing.
Phone: nav collapses to a menu, chips scroll sideways, grid drops to one column, the cart summary moves from beside the list to the end of it. Cart badge stays visible at every width.
